Name: Cloudflare Workers
Use Case: Low-latency request transformation and routing and API gateway at the edge
Strengths: Sub-millisecond cold start; 300+ edge locations; generous free tier; Workers KV for state
Weaknesses: Limited CPU time (10-50ms free/30s paid); no raw TCP sockets; V8 isolate limitations
Consistency Model: Eventual consistency (Workers KV); strong consistency with Durable Objects
Gotcha: Workers KV is eventually consistent with ~60s propagation — use Durable Objects for strong consistency

Name: Cloudflare Durable Objects
Use Case: Strongly consistent stateful logic at the edge — counters and sessions and coordination
Strengths: Single-threaded strong consistency per object; automatic geographic placement; WebSocket support
Weaknesses: Single-threaded limits throughput per object; pricing is per-request + duration; debugging is limited
Consistency Model: Strong consistency within an object; no cross-object transactions
Gotcha: Each Durable Object runs in one location — it's not replicated; latency depends on user distance to that location

Name: Fastly Compute
Runtime: WASM (any language that compiles to WASM)
Use Case: High-performance edge compute with language flexibility via WebAssembly
Strengths: Microsecond startup; WASM means any language (Rust/Go/JS); sub-ms TTFB; VCL compatibility
Weaknesses: Smaller edge network than Cloudflare; WASM ecosystem less mature than V8; limited local state
Gotcha: WASM binary size limits apply — keep dependencies minimal; Rust produces the smallest binaries

Name: AWS CloudFront Functions
Use Case: Simple request/response manipulation — header rewriting and URL redirects and A/B routing
Strengths: Sub-millisecond execution; runs on every CloudFront edge; very low cost; 2M free/month
Weaknesses: Extremely limited runtime (1ms max; 2MB code; no network calls; no file I/O); JavaScript only
Gotcha: CloudFront Functions cannot make network calls — use Lambda@Edge for anything beyond header manipulation

Name: AWS Lambda@Edge
Use Case: Full compute at CloudFront edge locations for dynamic content generation
Strengths: Full Lambda capabilities; up to 30s execution; network access; mature ecosystem
Weaknesses: Higher cold start than CF Functions (50-200ms); only runs at regional edge caches not all POPs; cost per request
Consistency Model: N/A — stateless (use DynamoDB Global Tables for state)
Gotcha: Lambda@Edge deploys to us-east-1 and replicates — all triggers must be in us-east-1; regional edge ≠ every POP

Name: Vercel Edge Functions
Use Case: Edge-rendered pages and API routes for Next.js applications
Strengths: Zero-config with Next.js; streaming support; global deployment; TypeScript native
Weaknesses: Tied to Vercel platform; limited CPU/memory; cold starts on free tier; vendor lock-in
Consistency Model: Eventual consistency for edge config; strong for KV (on paid plans)
Gotcha: Edge Functions have a 25ms CPU time limit on free tier — complex computation should use serverless functions instead

Name: Edge KV Stores
Use Case: Read-heavy key-value data at the edge — configuration and feature flags and A/B test assignments
Strengths: Global low-latency reads; CDN-integrated; simple key-value API
Weaknesses: Eventual consistency (seconds to minutes); limited query capabilities; size limits per value
Gotcha: Do not use edge KV for frequently-updated counters or inventory — eventual consistency causes overselling/double-counting

Name: WASI (WebAssembly System Interface)
Use Case: Portable and sandboxed server-side WebAssembly runtime for edge and beyond
Strengths: Language-agnostic; sandboxed security; portable across platforms; near-native performance
Weaknesses: Ecosystem still maturing; limited system call support in WASI preview 2; toolchain friction
Consistency Model: N/A — runtime standard not a data store
Gotcha: WASI preview 2 (component model) is the future but still stabilizing — preview 1 is more broadly supported today

Name: Edge Databases
Use Case: Full SQL database at the edge for read-heavy workloads with local-first semantics
Strengths: Sub-ms reads from local replica; SQL query support; offline capable
Weaknesses: Write propagation latency; conflict resolution complexity; storage limits
Consistency Model: Eventual consistency with automatic conflict resolution; some offer causal consistency
Gotcha: Edge databases with write support need conflict resolution — last-write-wins loses data; use CRDTs or app-level merge

Name: CDN as Compute Platform
Use Case: Using CDN infrastructure for compute not just caching — API responses and personalization and auth
Strengths: Massive global scale; low latency; reduces origin load
Weaknesses: Limited compute capabilities; debugging distributed edge is hard; vendor lock-in
Consistency Model: Depends on implementation — typically eventual consistency
Gotcha: Over-engineering at the edge adds latency from complexity — only move logic to edge if latency actually matters for that endpoint
